recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future tightening or narrowing of maxLength scope should be handled by a new work-group decision because later applied issues intentionally broadened support beyond string-only data.
issue_request: FHIR-20925 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core ElementDefinition. It asked that ElementDefinition.maxLength be prohibited for non-simple or complex types; the final 2019 resolution preferred clarifying the long description rather than adding an invariant and initially framed the clarification around strings.
initial_application: Commit fce5daa6e5be65acdae0d73ed5aa36503e75b532 explicitly applied FHIR-20925 by changing source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml to a string-oriented short description and adding that maxLength SHOULD only be used on primitive data types with a string representation.
additional_context: FHIR-22128 later reopened the same maxLength type-scope family and is already represented on the combined branch by b4e0f63158d8b5dfb2dc06497a562c836002c49f, which changed the current source to SHALL-only primitive data types where character length has meaning, not complex types such as Coding. FHIR-49226 later required date/dateTime/time support, so reverting to string-only wording would be wrong.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active ElementDefinition source already satisfies the seed's core requirement and no additional source edit is needed.
